headline: KEPCO confirmed exposure for 650,487 billing users and is still checking which procurement users had data exposed. Guadeloupe University Hospital postponed non-urgent care, while reporting on Fusionist estimated about $2 million in attacker proceeds and, separately, about $3.7 million in later bridge reserve withdrawals.

incidents.what: KEPCO confirmed exposure for 650,487 billing users and notified all 869,761 procurement users while it investigates the scope of the breach in that system.
The hospital director said encrypted databases and disrupted phones and clinical systems forced three sites to postpone non-urgent care.
The Block estimated about $2 million in attacker proceeds and separately valued later withdrawals from Fusionist’s bridge reserves at about $3.7 million.
Hyflock claimed it took data from Samsung Group; no independent confirmation was found.

incidents.org: Sri Lanka Department of Motor Traffic
incidents.what: The department said its public website was attacked but its separate appointment service stayed operational.
incidents.scale: Appointments unaffected; data exposure not disclosed

incidents.what: One X account alleged new unauthorized NES minting and estimated about $440,000 in sale proceeds; no independent or project confirmation was found.
Chainflip confirmed theft from two vaults and offered a recovery bounty; the combined dollar value is a media estimate, and no recovery was reported.
incidents.scale: About $12M estimated across Ethereum and Bitcoin

incidents.what: Rackspace restored its Spot console and urged affected customers to rotate cluster credentials after an intruder used leaked credentials to access some customer environments.
Voi Network published its account of the losses and said withdrawals stopped after Aramid secured the affected bridge accounts.
Cleverbridge confirmed stored payment-card data was copied; customer notices began November 20, and the number affected remains undisclosed.
incidents.scale: Card numbers and security codes; total unknown

incidents.what: Moats App’s post-mortem put losses from automated-rewards wallets at about $600,000 and said those wallets had been retired.
Follow-up coverage noted that Avo accepts cards from other banks and Nedbank has not identified which issuers’ cardholders were affected.
